newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia lead output to rise 14 percent - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australia lead output to rise 14 percent - ABARE.

text.p: Australian lead mine output is expected to rise by 14 percent in 1997/98 (July-June) mainly due to higher production from the Cannington mine in Queensland, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its June quarter Australian Commodities report.
Cannington is owned by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.

ABARE said Australian output is estimated to have risen by three percent in 1996/97, with increases at Normandy Mining Ltd's Woodcutters mine, MIM Holdings Ltd's McArthur River mine, both in the Northern Territory, Western Metal Ltd's Goongewa mine in Western Australia and
Aberfoyle Ltd's Hellyer mine in Tasmania.
The increases have been partly offset by lower production from the Hilton mine in Queensland owned by MIM.
Cannington began mining operations in May 1997 with first shipments of concentrate in January next year.

It was expected to reach full production by 1999 and would produce 175,000 tonnes of lead concentrate, equal to about six percent of world output, said ABARE, the government's chief commodities forecaster.

ABARE said Australian export earnings were expected to fall to A$451 million next financial year from A$467 million this year due to lower average prices which would more than offset higher export volumes of concentrate and refined lead.
Export earnings were estimated to have risen by 2.4 percent in 1996/97.

ABARE said the average world price of lead was forecast at US$670 a tonne in calendar 1997, about 13 percent less than in 1996, and was expected to fall by another six percent in 1998 as new mines came on stream.
Western world consumption was forecast to exceed production in 1997 but this would swing around in 1998 due to planned new mines such as Cannington.
World mine output was forecast to fall by 1.2 percent in 1997 and rise by 9.0 percent in 1998. Consumption was forecast to increase by 1.9 percent this calendar year and by 1.7 percent in 1998.
